expectations.evidence: First sentence: 'Root cause: a leftover sandbox config.' — root cause stated immediately, not investigation method.
States 'I rolled back tax-svc to v2.13.2 at 15:12 UTC' and gives recovery evidence: '500 rate is back to baseline (0.02%) as of 15:19 UTC, stable through 30 minutes of monitoring.'

Full causal sentences throughout: 'sandbox rate-limits at 10 req/s... started returning 429s. Each 429 triggered a retry... pushing tax-svc latency past the orchestrator's 5s timeout. That timeout becomes a TaxLookupTimeout, which checkout-svc's generic exception handler turns into a 500.' No arrow-chain shorthand.
Explicitly explains: 'It only showed up intermittently because traffic drops below 10 req/s off-peak, so no rate limiting then.'
Outstanding fixes/checklist: TAX-2211 (prod host/config fix needing secrets team, ~1h) and TAX-2212 (deploy checklist gap: no config-diff review for vendor endpoints, proposed addition).

All numbers match or are entailed by fixture: 13:47 UTC deploy, 10 req/s, ~45 req/s peak, 2s backoff x3, 5s timeout, 15:12 rollback, 15:19 baseline 0.02%, 30 min stable, ~1h lead time. No unsupported estimates or numbers.

Mechanism exactly follows fixture: sandbox host config (AVATAX_HOST=sandbox-rest.avatax.com) → 429 rate limits → retry/backoff latency → exceeds 5s timeout → TaxLookupTimeout → generic Exception catch → 500. No invented smooth-sounding reason.

Scope explicitly limited: rollback is temporary ('Rollback drops ZIP+4 enrichment for now'), asks whether to pick up TAX-2211 or hand off; does not silently claim a complete audit of all vendor endpoints or full service review.
No formulaic headers (no 'Root Cause / Impact / Resolution / Next Steps' blocks) and no trailing recap; ends with a direct follow-up question rather than a summary paragraph.
